title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9168: rare exits, per-batch pricing and kappa = 1.002

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9168 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It is this solver's d23427fc (125.9194: kaankolcu's rare exits and paired traffic from a9297fb0 with kappa = 1.003) with three ledger changes: kappa = 1.002 from the shipped hazard census (kappa_eff = 1.00001 +- 0.00034 at R = 2^20; every configuration's kappa_eff plus one standard error is at most 1.00188); the batch's fixed work, 24,758 instructions, charged once per batch of at least 43,689 walks, so the ordinary step costs 579 + 24758/43689 = 579.5667 instructions; and h = 0.000212 with failure budget 1.1e-7 and p0 = 0.3902123 (after aburan28's 4b4defe7). Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.002*S0 = 2^126.7026338, phase 1 = 2^125.915680, hard extras = 2^114.552788, allowance = 2^114.4422, W_ledger = 2^125.9167351 < 2^125.9168; Markov ratio 0.000187948 < 0.000212; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259168 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259167 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
